He narrowed down the group to those believed to be British airmen.
"We were looking at a group of seven skulls and I noticed all these holes throughout the squamosal portion of the skull - you could see what looked like a saw cuts on the surface," Det Sgt Horn said.

"We tried to put the two groups together, but could not because they didn't fit together. It wasn't until a week or so later they pulled one of the remains out because they were all buried and we got to look properly at the rest of the body," he said.
